name.description: Logical agent identity; maps to config.Identity.

instance.description: Specific running instance of the named agent.

request.description: Correlation tag of the originating request; every reply echoes it. It names one turn and must not be reused for another. A task binding may make it part of the address the process running that task listens on, so the character set and the length are constrained.

conversation.description: Stable across multiple requests in a session.

parent.description: Causation: the request that spawned this one, for multi-hop A->B->C.

sequence.description: Per-request, gap-free, monotonic ordering authority. Never reused across a restart.

time.description: Advisory/audit only; not an ordering authority.

must_understand.description: If true and the receiver does not understand this protocol id, it must fail closed.

traceparent.description: W3C trace context of the span that sent this message, so a receiver's spans join the sender's trace. Named here rather than constrained: a version pattern would refuse a valid future W3C version and cost the whole message, where a receiver's propagator already ignores anything it cannot parse. Unauthenticated, like sender.

usage.description: What a task consumed. Tokens are what it cost; calls are what it did.

input_tokens.description: Total input tokens, cached and uncached together. The cache fields below break it down, since they bill at different rates.

cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens served from the prompt cache, included in input_tokens.

cache_create_tokens.description: Input tokens written into the prompt cache, included in input_tokens.

thinking_tokens.description: Output tokens the model spent reasoning, included in output_tokens.

llm_calls.description: How many times the agent called the model.

tool_calls.description: How many tools the agent invoked.

budget.description: Mirrors LLMBudget. The receiver's local config is the ceiling; a request may only lower a limit.

stop_reason.description: Why a task ended. This version names end_turn, max_tokens, refusal, canceled, error, budget_exhausted, suspended and max_iterations. A reason outside that set is accepted rather than refused, since rejecting one would cost the whole terminal message including the answer text; it is bounded because a receiver displays it.

conversation_token.description: Handle for a conversation, minted by the answering agent and carried on its ack. A later request carrying it runs its prompt as the next turn of that conversation. It is a credential rather than an id: holding it is the authorization to add a turn, so a receiver neither logs nor displays it.

stream.description: false means the caller wants only a terminal result, no event stream.

deltas.description: true asks for the text and reasoning of an assistant turn as the model writes it, as text_delta and thinking_delta events alongside the whole blocks. It has no meaning without stream, since a fragment is an event. A worker that predates it ignores it and sends whole blocks.

force.description: Continue a conversation whose stored fingerprint no longer matches the worker's configuration, which is otherwise refused. Standing approvals that cannot be vouched for across the change are dropped.

replay.description: Open the reply set with this many blocks of the stored conversation, counted back from the end, before the first new event. The worker rounds outwards to a turn boundary and caps what it sends.

answer.description: What an operator said, for a question whose run has ended. It carries its own kind and answer because it is a field of a request rather than a message with an id of its own.

kind.description: The question that was asked, taken from the question. It says what the answer means where the answer value alone cannot, since no_operator is the same value for all four.

answer.description: Which field below carries the answer. A selection names the option it chose rather than a position, the run that offered the list having ended, and there is no waiting here: nobody is holding a question open.

question_id.description: Correlates a question and its answer. Unique within the task. An answer naming a question the task did not ask is dropped.

tool_use_id.description: The tool call a question is about, which is what an answer given after the run has ended names: a resume asks the question again under a new question_id, so the call is what both ends agree on. Absent from an agent that takes no answer once its run has ended.

wait_ms.description: How long a question is held open before the agent gives up on it, in milliseconds. A caller with a person in front of the question sends an elicit waiting message every third of it to restart it. Absent is an agent that predates this and takes no such messages, as is a 400 in answer to one; answer inside the window instead.

elicit_question.description: The text to put to the operator. Model-supplied and sanitized before sending; sanitize again for your own surface.

elicit_options.description: The choices a select question offers, in the order to show them. The reply answers with a position in this list.

elicit_choice.description: Answers an approve question. once authorizes the one call that asked; always covers that tool for the rest of the conversation. no leaves the command unrun and tells the model the refusal is final.

elicit_value.description: A free text answer. An empty string is a valid answer, which is why the protocol id rather than emptiness says what was given. Bounded because it is third-party input that reaches a model and a terminal.

exec_result.description: Optional command metadata, mirroring CommandResult; absent for non-shell tools.

tool_descriptor.description: A tool an agent exposes, as reported in a discovery reply.

input_schema.description: JSON schema for the tool input.

tool_behavior.description: What the serving agent says calling a tool does to the world. Every property is a hint the serving agent asserts about its own tool, never a guarantee, and an absent property asserts nothing.

read_only.description: The call does not modify its environment.

destructive.description: The call may destroy or overwrite existing state rather than only adding to it. Meaningful only when the call is not read-only.

idempotent.description: Repeating the call with the same arguments has no further effect. Meaningful only when the call is not read-only.

open_world.description: The call reaches an open set of external entities rather than a closed one the operator configured.

block_index.description: Where this block sat in the model call that produced it, counted over every block of that call including the ones that never reach the wire. It pairs with the index of the delta blocks that carried this block's fragments; those also name the model call, and this does not. Omitting it when unset makes absent mean both the first block and a worker that predates the field, which costs nothing: a receiver that asked for no deltas has nothing to reconcile.

block_trimmed.description: The text was cut to 64 KiB and the rest of it is only in the serving worker's run journal. A receiver holding delta fragments of this block needs it: the fragments were never capped in aggregate, so for a long answer they are the more complete copy.

thinkingBlock.description: Each block definition below is referenced by the event schema of one protocol id. What kind of block it is travels as that id, so nothing in the block itself names its kind.

signature.description: Opaque, provider-defined; display/audit only, never replayed into a model across the boundary.

provider.description: Originating provider for the signature, e.g. anthropic.

final.description: Marks the text of the turn that ended the run, which is the answer rather than narration on the way to it. The same text arrives again in the result.

textDeltaBlock.description: One fragment of a text block as the model writes it. The whole block follows when the model call ends, carrying the same index, so a fragment adds to it and never replaces it. It carries no iteration: a receiver takes the call from the status blocks it has already seen. Sent only to a caller that asked for deltas.

index.description: The position of this fragment's block in the model call that produced it. Fragments of different blocks may interleave, so a receiver keys its buffer on this rather than assuming one block finishes before the next begins.

iteration.description: The model call this fragment came from, 1-based, counted as a status block counts it. Indices restart at 0 on every call and the status block separating two calls arrives after the first has ended, so a receiver keying on index alone would append the first block of one call to the last block of the one before. A worker that does not report it leaves it absent.

text.description: This fragment's text, appended to what has already arrived for the same iteration and index. Absent on a final fragment with nothing left to send.

final.description: The last fragment of this block, so a receiver closes the buffer when the block ends rather than holding its tail until the next fragment or the end of the run. The end of a block cannot be read off the fragments themselves.

thinkingDeltaBlock.description: One fragment of a thinking block's reasoning as the model writes it, on the terms textDeltaBlock states. The signature does not stream; it arrives with the whole block.

index.description: The position of this fragment's block in the model call that produced it, as it is on a text delta.

iteration.description: The model call this fragment came from, 1-based, as it is on a text delta.

text.description: This fragment's reasoning text, appended to what has already arrived for the same iteration and index.

final.description: The last fragment of this block, as it is on a text delta.

call_id.description: The id of the tool_call this answers.

is_error.description: Harness failure (tool did not run cleanly), distinct from a non-zero exit.

agentCallBlock.description: A call to another agent (multi-hop), distinct from a local tool call.

task.description: request id of the spawned sub-task; correlate its stream via the header `parent`.

phase.description: e.g. calling-llm, executing-tool. replay_start and replay_end bracket a stored conversation a resume was asked to replay.

usage.description: On an iteration status, what that one model call consumed. On replay_end, what the stored conversation has consumed in total, so a caller can seed a running count before this turn's own calls arrive. The two are not summed.

count.description: On replay_end, how many blocks of the stored conversation were sent.

truncated.description: On replay_end, whether older blocks were left behind.

promptBlock.description: A turn somebody asked for: the prompt a conversation opened with, or one added to it later. A live run never sends one; it appears when a stored conversation is replayed.

warningBlock.description: An advisory the run raised. It carries the warning rather than a sentence about it, so the wording belongs to whatever renders it.

kind.description: What the warning is about, as a string. A receiver that does not know a kind still has the other fields.

name.description: The tool, key or setting the warning is about.

error.description: The failure the warning reports, as display text. Never matched on.
